focus: The History Lookup CLI's own failure surface
noveltyJustification: 6 of 8 findings were new; the claim-time mint and the checkout check restated earlier evidence with the withholding conditions enumerated.
ruledOut: A withheld offer is visible to the receiver

graphEvents.label: The CLI refuses a locator older than 30 minutes
The mint withholds the offer on six distinct conditions
A withheld offer is silent because the call site catches and prints nothing

label: The CLI refuses a locator older than 30 minutes: LOCATOR_TTL_MS is 30 minutes and isFresh requires a non-negative age below it.
A locator whose mintedAt is in the future counts as stale, because a future timestamp is clock skew rather than freshness.
The mint is done at claim time rather than prepare time precisely because of the TTL, so a note claimed hours later still redeems.

mintHandoverLocator returns null on an empty runtime or session id, a runtime with no locator kind, a missing transcript path, a placeLookup miss, a reader that cannot find the session, or a recorded folder outside the sender's checkout.
For Pi and OpenCode the mint asks the reader directly instead of resolving a transcript path, so the mint and the lookup agree on whether the session exists.
The offer is withheld unless the receiver's workspace and the sender's workspace are the same checkout, because the printed command moves to the locator's workspace.
lookupRunsFrom requires a .git entry, the entry script and the compiled core at history/dist/cli.js, so a checkout without a built core gets no offer at all.
Every withholding condition fails closed by returning null and the claim command wraps the call in a bare catch, so a withheld offer produces no message, no log line and no marker.

direction: A withheld offer is visible to the receiver
reason: The claim output prints the section only when non-null and the surrounding catch swallows any error, so absence is silent.
Minting at claim time makes the TTL irrelevant to a normal hop; it only bites a locator minted and redeemed across a long gap.
